DEFINITION · qeva:1:operation@2

Operation

An operation is a typed map from declared input sorts to a declared output sort.

editorialfoundations · algebra
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

An operation takes inputs of declared kinds and returns an output of a declared kind; not every useful operation is closed on one set.

EXACT

The compact statement

An n-ary typed operation is a function ω:X₁×⋯×Xₙ→Y. It is internal on X when X₁=⋯=Xₙ=Y=X. An external operation, such as scalar multiplication F×V→V, may have different input and output sorts.

Example

Integer addition Z×Z→Z is internal; scalar multiplication F×V→V is heterogeneous.

Boundary / caveat

Partial, relational, multivalued, stochastic, and higher operations require additional structure beyond this total-function formulation.

Assumptions

  • Every input and output sort is declared. · Function @1
